sample_unit: patient questions (chatbot responses rated by expert)

links.outcome: Correctness, completeness, and harm of RAG-grounded GPT-4 answers rated against guidelines
links.effect: 91 (87.5%) rated correct, 72 (69.2%) complete, 93 (89.4%) nonharmful; 6 (5.8%) potentially harmful due to outdated or contextually inappropriate recommendations. No comparison without grounding.
links.quote: Among the 104 responses assessed for the remaining dimensions, 91 (87.5%) were rated as correct, 72 (69.2%) as complete, and 93 (89.4%) as nonharmful.

links.outcome: Outdated or incomplete guideline content in chatbot answers
links.effect: Incomplete answers omitted updates from recent therapeutic guidelines; 6 (5.8%) answers rated potentially harmful due to outdated or contextually inappropriate recommendations.
links.quote: In addition, 6 (5.8%) of the answers were rated as potentially harmful due to outdated or contextually inappropriate recommendations.

screen.reason: The study develops and tests a customized GPT-4 RAG system on authentic patient questions evaluated offline by an expert and patient representatives, but it does not compare outcomes with vs without a specific organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
